subject: maths
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE Mathematics specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Assessment structure (two completion units)
units.blurb: Sit one unit from M1–M4 and one from M5–M8

topics.name: Sit one unit from M1–M4 and one from M5–M8

connections.why: Algebra generalises the arithmetic and structure of number
Measurement and mensuration calculations rely on numerical skills
Coordinate geometry and formulae link algebra to geometry and measures
Averages, spread and probability are computed using numerical methods
Lines of best fit and their equations interpret bivariate data
Statistical diagrams and scatter graphs use coordinate and graphing skills
Higher-tier units extend the same content domains assessed at foundation tier
The foundation pairing is one valid route through the two-unit completion structure
The higher pairing is the alternative route through the two-unit completion structure
Foundation completion units assess the number and data content domains
Higher completion units assess the more demanding algebra content domain
Higher units assess extended geometry and trigonometry content
